pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Revises B.G. Shirke Construction Technology’s Outlook to Positive; Affirms ‘IND A’
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has revised B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) Outlook to Positive from Stable while affirming its Long-Term Issuer Rating at ‘IND A’. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows:
overviewHTML:
Ind-Ra continues to consider BGSCPTL’s standalone financials to arrive at the ratings and has not consolidated the amount of guarantee extended to its related parties such as B G Shirke Redevelopment and Gas Pvt. Ltd. (BGSRGPL), Parijat Hill View Realty LLP (PHVR) and Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP. (TSRLLP). However, Ind-Ra has factored in the debt guaranteed of these entities and the likelihood of any incremental support required by these entities to arrive at the ratings.

The Positive Outlook reflects Ind-Ra’s expectation of healthy revenue growth given BGSCPTL’s declined-but-strong order book of 3.1x of FY22 revenue and healthy EBITDA margins over the near term. Furthermore Ind-Ra expects the credit metrics to remain comfortable with the generation of positive cash flow from operations of over INR2.2 billion in the near-to-medium term.
keyRatingDrivers:
Strong Operating Performance:  BGSCPTL’s revenue grew at a robust 39% yoy to INR43.9 billion in FY22, due to the strong execution of its order book and an increase in the contribution from its shipping segment. BGSCTPL’s order book from construction contracts, which is the main line of business, stood strong at INR124.15 billion at end-May 2022 (FY21: INR155 billion), providing an order book visibility of 3.1x of its FY22 revenue (FY21: 5.3x). Although the order inflow was low yoy in FY22 on account of COVID-19, Ind-Ra expects  it to pick up in FY23 with an acceleration of activity in the construction sector and since the company’s active bidding pipeline under consideration is over INR59 billion. The company won orders worth INR8.7 billion in July 2022. Ind-Ra expects the revenue growth to continue in FY23 with the company likely to earn a revenue of INR4.4 billion-4.6 billion. The absolute EBITDA increased to INR6.7 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR5.3 billion) on account of the revenue increase. However, BGSCTPL’s EBITDA margins moderated to 15.4% in FY22 from 16.8% in FY21, due to an increase in the material costs (FY22: 64% of revenue; FY21: 60%). The management expects the company to maintain similar margins over the near term.

Robust Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL's net leverage (net on-balance sheet debt/operating EBITDAR) reduced to 0.9x in FY22 (FY21: 1.4x) and its gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) increased to 4.5x (3.7x) due to a rise in the EBITDA and a reduction in the on-balance sheet debt to INR10.5 billion (INR11.3 billion). In FY22, BGSCTPL extended a corporate guarantee of INR0.627 billion to group companies (FY21: INR0.404 billion). The company’s net adjusted leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDAR) stood at 0.9x in FY22 (FY21: 1.4x).  Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s net leverage to increase to 1.3x in FY23 on account of it incurring a capex to purchase two ships before improving to below 1x FY24 onwards. 

Liquidity Indicator - Adequate: BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents of INR4.7 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR4.2 billion). Moreover, over the 12 months ended June 2022, the average maximum utilisation of the company’s fund-based working capital limits stood at 52%, and the utilisation of its non-fund-based limits was 56%. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks, with limited presence of private banks. The on-balance sheet debt of INR10.5 billion at FYE21 comprised terms loan amounting to INR4.3 billion, intercorporate and deposits from related parties worth INR1.2 billion and working capital loans of INR5.0 billion. The company has scheduled repayments of INR1.9 billion and INR1.3 billion in FY23 and FY24, respectively. 

Healthy Free Cash Flow: BGSCTPL’s cash flow from operations increased  to INR2.45 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR 2.03 billion) , given the increase in its absolute EBITDA on account of higher execution of projects. There was an increase in net working capital requirement to INR2.7 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR2.1 billion) on account of an increase in the inventory and a decrease in mobilisation advances. The mobilisation advances from Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) and City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) do not entail an interest pay-out, while those from Delhi Development Authority (DDA)  carry an interest. The company's capex spend declined to INR1.2 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR1.6 billion), which led to an increase  in the free cash flow to INR1.3 billion (INR0.4 billion). BGSCTPL is likely to incur a capex of INR5 billion-6 billion in FY23 for acquiring ships and a capex of INR2 billion each year over the near term. 

Increasing Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL extended corporate guarantees and letters of undertaking worth INR0.62 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR0.40 billion) to group entities. Also, BGSCTPL extends loans and advances to BGSRGPL, which increased to INR4.05 billion in FY22 (FY21: INR3.47 billion). Shirke Recreation Enterprise, Shirke Club Management LLP, , PHVR and BGSRGPL together accounted for 88% of the total loans and advances in FY22. BGSRGPL had an outstanding debt of INR3,450 million at FYE22, for which BGSCTPL has extended a corporate guarantee and has kept in lien an equivalent amount of fixed deposit. There was an increase the loans and advances in BGSRGPL in FY22 on account of it undertaking three redevelopment projects; this will further increase over the near term. However, BGSCTPL will see its loans and advances decrease from TSRLLP and PHVR as both projects are completed and have started selling flats.

Customer and Regional Concentration in Order Book Remains High: BGSCPTL’s order book is concentrated in terms of segmental as  well as customer base. CIDCO, DDA and MHADA, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and Pimpri Chinchwad New Town Development Authority accounted for 38%, 31%, 9%, 6%, respectively, of its total order book at end-May 2022. The concentration of the top 10 projects in the order book at end-May 2022 remained high at 69% (end-May 2021: 71%). The orders from Mumbai Metropolitan Region account for 60% of the order book, followed by those from Delhi (16%), Pune, Nagpur and Nashik (14%), Southern India (9%) and others 1%. BGSCTPL continues to focus on the prefabricated housing industry, wherein the company has a track record of over 30 years.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: A consistent increase in the revenue, along with the sustenance of profitability and the net adjusted leverage remaining below 1.25x on a sustained basis while maintaining/reducing the support provided to the group companies will be positive for the ratings.

Outlook revision to Stable: A decline in the profitability or an increase in the net adjusted leverage above 1.25x on a sustained basis will be negative for ratings.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as DDA, MHADA, CIDCO and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. The company also has presence in other segments such as shipping, aviation and post-harvest equipment.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
